thread.title: Homeland Security Throws Apple and Amazon a Bone on Hacking Report

title: Homeland Security Throws Apple and Amazon a Bone on Hacking Report
text:
Homeland Security Throws Apple and Amazon a Bone on Hacking Report By Updated Oct. 8, 2018 10:45 a.m. ET Order Reprints Print Article People purchase the new iPhone XS and XS Max at the Apple store in New York City. Getty Images Text size
The U.S. Department of Homeland Security says it has no reason not to believe Apple (AAPL), Amazon (AMZN), and other companies that have denied a Bloomberg Businessweek report that Chinese intelligence services inserted malicious computer chips into their equipment.
“The Department of Homeland Security is aware of the media reports of a technology supply chain compromise,” DHS said in a statement over the weekend. “Like our partners in the UK, the National Cyber Security Centre, at this time we have no reason to doubt the statements from the companies named in the story.”
On Sunday, Apple upped the ante. Its vice president for information security, George Stathakopoulos, wrote in a letter to Congress that it found no evidence of tampering. “Apple’s proprietary security tools are continuously scanning for precisely this kind of outbound traffic, as it indicates the existence of malware or other malicious activity,” he wrote. “Nothing was ever found.”
Bloomberg, citing more than a dozen intelligence and company sources, reported Thursday that Chinese spies placed tiny spy chips inside motherboards and other equipment used by about 30 companies and U.S. government agencies to gain secret access to internal networks.
